subject: history
title: Medieval & Early Modern Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the key words and events from 1066 to 1750 — kings, peasants, plague and reform.
meta_desc: GCSE History Medieval & Early Modern foundations — Norman Conquest, feudalism, Black Death, Magna Carta and the Reformation.
final_note: You learned the core vocabulary and big events of medieval and early modern England.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1066 William of Normandy defeated King Harold at the Battle of Hastings.

William built castles, brought French-speaking lords and set up the feudal system — land in exchange for loyalty and soldiers.

In 1215 rebel barons forced King John to seal Magna Carta — the king must obey the law.

In 1348-49 the Black Death killed roughly a third of England. Fewer workers meant peasants could demand better pay.

Henry VIII broke from Rome in the 1530s — the start of the English Reformation.

By 1649 Parliament executed Charles I in the English Civil War. England briefly became a republic under Oliver Cromwell.

mcqs.q: Who won the Battle of Hastings in 1066?
options: Harold Godwinson
William of Normandy
Edward the Confessor
Harald Hardrada

mcqs.q: What did Magna Carta mainly do?
options: Crowned a new king
Limited the king's power
Started the Reformation
Ended the Black Death

mcqs.q: What did Magna Carta actually do in 1215?
options: It was a peace treaty between King John and rebel barons protecting baronial privileges and limiting arbitrary royal taxation and imprisonment — it was annulled within months.
Magna Carta gave ordinary English people democratic rights and freedom.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
It was a list of Anglo-Saxon rebels William wanted to execute.

mcqs.q: Why did William of Normandy claim the English throne in 1066?
options: Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
He claimed Edward the Confessor had promised him the throne in 1051 and that Harold Godwinson had sworn an oath to support that claim in 1064.
William invaded because he was the strongest king in Europe and wanted more land.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.

mcqs.q: Why did William the Conqueror commission the Domesday Book in 1086?
options: It was a list of Anglo-Saxon rebels William wanted to execute.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
It was a census of the English population, like a modern one.
To record landholding and resources so he could assess taxation (geld), confirm Norman tenants' rights, and settle disputes over confiscated Anglo-Saxon estates.
